Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness band like the WHOOP or Fitbit Air. I've been using WHOOP for six months and genuinely think this direction makes sense, but there are a few areas where I hope Apple can do a better job.

Since the product is still in the early stages of development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screenless fitness band, and it may not launch until 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric wristband with built-in sensors and a computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer discounts or free WHOOP devices to Sapphire credit card holders — I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around that time, but I never managed to fully commit to using it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection has never been perfect, and I find it a hassle to deliberately pull out my phone to log a workout — whether before or after exercise. Apple Watch can start tracking directly from the watch face, and WHOOP can sync timing through Apple Health. This is also the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm working out at the gym, pulling out my phone is still acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or strolling, I don't want to deliberately take out my phone just to log the activity.

So for Apple's screenless fitness band, I sincerely hope they can include a combination of buttons and indicator lights to start and stop workout recording. You'd still need to use your phone afterward to categorize the activity type, but I'd rather handle that after the workout than deal with so many things during exercise. Apple could also develop categorization models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully create a screenless fitness band that's easy to use and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This design has several advantages, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Speaking personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I actually still lean more toward wearing a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand that some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's Do Not Disturb mode solves that problem.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness band? How much would you be willing to pay for it? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
